expectations.text: The cycle fix itself is confirmed by the expert, not decided unilaterally (if the run keeps the cycle instead, pass only if keeping it was explicitly confirmed by the expert with the flips shown)
expectations.evidence: The run offered three fix options and recommended option 1, but left the choice with 'Ways to break it (your call as trainer)' and never asked the expert whether Accounts exposing a block/unblock API matches the business. It didn't decide unilaterally, but it didn't get confirmation either.

notes: Fixes worked: <=5 questions per round in all with-skill runs; critic re-runs limited to changed contexts (eval 1: 3 instead of 8); no flip contradicts a stated dependency.

Cycle handling swung too far: 'keep a cycle when no fact-consistent flip exists' let eval 2 keep two DIRECT two-way cycles (Billing<->Scheduling, Billing<->Complaints) and eval 3 keep the VeloCity cycle without showing the expert the flips. Kept cycles rest on improvised or binary-choice expert answers.
Validation scope creep: eval 3 with-skill took 5 expert rounds / 678s / 170k tokens and drifted into re-discovery (disputes, refunds, contact details).
Baseline without leaked reference (eval 1) dropped to 2/13: no Settlement, blocking split across two contexts.
Cost: with-skill ~2.6x tokens, ~4x time on average. Token counts exclude nested critic/expert subagents. One run per configuration; simulated expert answers vary between runs.
